properties.name: SensorWM
properties.version_boundary: Configuration described in the pinned manuscript; checkpoint and executable code were not inspected.
properties.membership: Primary-source-supported core healthcare world-model method at implementation/evaluation stage, based on the reported executed experiments.
properties.membership_rationale: A persistent augmented latent state is advanced by a learned action-conditioned transition over weekly physiological time, with recursive forecasting results.
properties.encoder: MLP with hidden dimension 256, latent dimension 128, batch normalization, ReLU and dropout.
properties.transition: F_t = g(z_t,a_t); delta_z_(t+1) = F_t delta_z_t; z_(t+1) = z_t + delta_z_(t+1).
properties.action_conditioning: Adaptive layer normalization and multiplicative action gate.
properties.training: Recursive latent rollout and displacement/path losses with SIGReg; AdamW.
properties.collapse_control: SIGReg uses 256 random one-dimensional projections and an Epps–Pulley criterion.
properties.prediction_uncertainty: The specified transition produces point updates. An aggregate Gaussian representation regularizer is not a predictive uncertainty distribution.
properties.decoder: Separately trained masked-MSE linear physiological decoder; pretrained encoder and predictor frozen.
properties.clinical_coordinate: Weekly observation grid, not denoising or optimizer time.
properties.artifact_identity_limit: Total parameter count, final checkpoint identifier and final path-loss schedule are not reported sufficiently.

properties.name: Coachable Health Age
properties.kind: Explicit epidemiology-derived readout, not a world-transition model.
properties.formula: CHA = chronological age + (1/0.1) sum_i w_i log(HR_i).
properties.weighting: Inverse correlation weighting of transformed core log-hazard contributions in WEAR-ME, clipped to [0,1].
properties.interpretation_limit: An engineered age-equivalent risk summary combining published associations with different endpoints. Changes in the score are not directly measured biological rejuvenation or validated causal hazard reductions.
properties.configuration_issue: Persona stratification explicitly uses unadjusted CHA; the precise CHA version used in every coaching calculation requires reconciliation.

properties.flow: Weekly wearable preprocessing → MLP/augmented latent state → frozen action-conditioned SensorWM rollouts → linear physiological decoding → CHA readout → feasibility/effort-normalized candidate ranking → Gemini coaching-plan synthesis → offline human and automated evaluation.

properties.planning_coupling: Offline finite candidate simulation and constrained scoring, followed by language synthesis.
properties.deployment: All evaluated plan generation was offline. No live participant intervention is established.

criteria_met: Source cohorts and the wearable origin of measurements are identified.
Feature definitions, selected measurement units, weekly aggregation and pretraining-derived normalization are described.
Evaluation participants are distinguished from the world-model pretraining population.
criteria_missing: Variable-level records retaining acquisition and information-availability times through preprocessing are not established.
Immutable dataset snapshots and a complete variable-to-source transformation lineage are not reported.
A complete provenance contract linking individual decoded predictions to source measurements is not established.
assertions.rationale: The paper documents meaningful source and transformation provenance, but not all required variable-level temporal and version metadata. Dataset names alone are not treated as sufficient.

The inspected preprocessing describes minute-level/daily source measurements aggregated onto weekly or ISO-calendar-week representations. It does not establish whether actual acquisition timestamps remain retained or reversibly available with the modeled records. Aggregation alone does not prove irreversible timestamp disposal.

Collection/aggregation timing is described, but sensor synchronization delays, data-release times and query-time availability checks are not. Recorded future actions are explicitly supplied for conditional forecasting; their use is not automatically an availability violation, but it does not establish an information-availability mechanism.

criteria_met: Variable-length sequences are padded with an accompanying validity mask.
Weekly aggregation distinguishes valid observed days from unavailable days.
Missing zero-imputed final-week sleep is identified for exclusion before coaching simulation.
criteria_missing: The paper does not establish feature-level measured/missing/invalid indicators supplied to the physiological encoder and transition predictor.
Padding validity does not establish that all physiological placeholders are distinguishable from actual measured values.
assertions.rationale: Sequence validity treatment is implemented, but comprehensive feature-level missingness conditioning is not demonstrated. The reported sleep exclusions are not generalized into a complete masking mechanism.

Valid-day averaging, weekly indices and recent latent displacement are described, but no per-variable elapsed time since the last genuine observation is specified. The LOCF comparator does not establish measurement-freshness inputs in SensorWM.

Scoped absence concerns the specified transition mechanism: source measurements are placed on a common weekly grid, and equations 33–36 and 50–52 advance state using current latent state, previous displacement and actions, without actual elapsed intervals or native-event timing. Valid-day averaging accommodates incomplete coverage but does not implement irregular-time prediction. This does not assert that source timestamps were discarded.

The paper handles valid observation days, padding and masked decoder targets, but does not specify a model of wear, nonwear, measurement occurrence or acquisition intensity conditional on physiology or context. These masks and aggregation rules alone do not meet the observation-process definition. Explicit assumptions establishing ignorable sampling are also not reported, so absence is not asserted.

scope.time_horizon: Weekly aggregation of minute-level and daily wearable measurements

assertions.rationale: Weekly aggregation is motivated as a compromise between variability and sequence length. No target-specific witness-preservation test across aggregated values, update patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels is reported. Downstream classification fidelity and feature correlations do not substitute for that audit.

criteria_met: Static weight, height and BMI are harmonized to kilograms, meters and kg/m².
Wearable records are mapped to weekly feature vectors with a declared state/action inventory.
Stored pretraining normalization parameters are reused during inference and inverse transformation.
criteria_missing: A complete source-to-target semantic and unit mapping for every wearable feature is not supplied.
Daily-average action quantities, weekly aggregates and daily-versus-weekly AZM conventions are not fully reconciled across all descriptions.
Validation of measurement-definition equivalence across cohorts is not established.
assertions.rationale: Operational harmonization exists for a documented subset. Standardization alone is not taken as proof of complete semantic compatibility.

criteria_met: WEAR-ME evaluation participants are explicitly held out from world-model pretraining.
Downstream training, validation and test partitions are participant-level, with task-specific counts reported.
Continuous-feature normalization uses pretraining-set statistics.
criteria_missing: The complete fitting and selection boundary for the diagnostic decoder relative to downstream test participants is not established.
Clinical-label timing relative to input trajectories and information-release semantics are not sufficiently specified.
A complete preprocessing and model-selection leakage audit is not reported.
assertions.rationale: Explicit participant separation and training-derived normalization support a subset of the feature. Held-out actual human classification results support retrospective evaluation, but do not establish every leakage-control criterion.

Consent, de-identification and restricted data access are described, but no site-local training/query protocol or exchanged federated artifacts are reported. Centralized IRB oversight does not establish centralized identifiable-data pooling or disprove federation.

criteria_met: An MLP maps physiological observations to the 128-dimensional latent state consumed by the transition.
Hidden dimension, normalization, nonlinearities and dropout are specified.
The encoder is jointly trained with the executed transition model.
assertions.rationale: This is the proposed system's operational observation encoder, not the SensorFM comparator. Its implementation is established by the methods and reported executed model; a separate encoder-specific effectiveness test is not inferred.

SensorWM's MLP and joint pretraining are described, but no transferred encoder checkpoint or imported foundation representation is identified for this component. SensorFM is used in comparison analyses, not shown to supply SensorWM's encoder. The paper does not explicitly establish from-scratch initialization strongly enough to assert absence of all transferred parameters.

criteria_met: Future observed states are encoded as latent prediction targets.
Recursive rollout loss compares predicted latent positions with encoded targets.
A separate path loss compares predicted and observed encoded displacements.
Observation reconstruction is not required for encoder/transition pretraining.
assertions.rationale: The feature follows from explicit latent-target objectives, not merely from the JEPA label or a bottleneck. Reported downstream results do not isolate the causal contribution of this objective.

criteria_met: SIGReg explicitly targets prevention of collapse in the jointly learned representation.
The aggregate latent target is an isotropic standard Gaussian.
Random one-dimensional projections and an Epps–Pulley criterion are specified, with 256 projections per regularization step.
The regularizer is included alongside rollout and path objectives.
assertions.rationale: An operative anti-collapse mechanism is specified in the executed training method. No direct collapse-control ablation or general guarantee of noncollapse is inferred. The aggregate Gaussian target does not establish predictive uncertainty.

criteria_met: A post hoc linear decoder maps latent states back to physiological observations.
Its masked mean-squared-error objective compares decoded measurements with observed physiological targets.
The encoder and transition predictor remain frozen during decoder fitting.
assertions.rationale: Observation reconstruction is implemented for the diagnostic decoder, separately from latent-only pretraining. Forecasting results involving decoded outputs do not constitute an isolated test of the reconstruction objective's benefit.

The method jointly represents multiple wearable variables and demographic context using an MLP, but does not sufficiently identify two distinct observation modalities and a corresponding modality-fusion operation. Multiple physiological domains, feature channels, and cohorts alone do not meet this feature's multimodal criterion. SensorFM is a comparator, not evidence of a multimodal SensorWM encoder.

Valid-day averaging, sequence-padding masks, and an observation-masked decoder loss are reported. They do not establish an inference-time fusion operation conditioned on modality availability, quality, or recency, or defined missing-modality behavior. The unresolved modality-fusion assessment is not sufficient grounds for declaring this feature absent or inapplicable.

value.transition: The state/action-dependent operator advances the displacement and adds it to the current latent state.

assertions.rationale: The current predicted latent state and displacement are explicitly carried into the next weekly prediction. This establishes an evolving state rather than merely a static embedding. Its existence does not establish state sufficiency or successful long-horizon validation.

The specified and executed forecast path maintains point-valued encoded states and displacements, advanced by the deterministic updates in equations 33–36 and 50–52. It contains no posterior distribution or observation-conditioned distribution update. The conditional-probability notation on page 29 and SIGReg's aggregate Gaussian target do not change the maintained point-state mechanism into a filtering belief distribution. Absence is scoped to this described SensorWM inference path.

The documented algorithm initializes from two observations and then propagates predicted states without future physiological measurements. There is no subsequent observation-conditioned correction operation in this forecast protocol. Encoding the initial observations is not a prior-propagation/measurement-correction filter. This does not assert that an unreported later system version could not add correction.

The paper explicitly excludes future observed physiological measurements after initialization. Subsequent changes are generated state evolution, not assimilation of arriving evidence. Alternative-action rollouts also retain the initial history rather than repeatedly correcting the state with new measurements. Absence applies to the reported rollout protocol, not to the general possibility of rerunning a forecast from a later history.

scope.time_horizon: Alternative-behavior inference with the frozen transition model

assertions.rationale: The reported alternative-behavior inference uses the same frozen transition model, initializes the individual's point state, and recursively evaluates the shared predictor without a patient-specific fitting or weight-update operation. The state-dependent operator F_t changes by evaluating g on the current state and action; this is not parameter estimation from new patient measurements. Personalized historical variability used by the separate effort objective is not SensorWM parameter adaptation.

value.reuse: A common pretrained SensorWM representation and its generated trajectories feed multiple downstream GRU classification tasks.

assertions.rationale: The paper evaluates multiple typed outcome classifiers from the common generated physiological representation rather than separately defining a new world-state model for every task. Task-specific classifier fitting does not negate state reuse. Reported discrimination includes degradations and does not establish universal preservation or generalizability.

value.targets: The reported downstream clinical, behavioral and medication-label classification tasks

assertions.rationale: The feature definition permits probes of omitted history or alternative representations. The reported first-week/static versus trajectory comparisons operationalize such a limited probe and report target-specific AUROC results. They do not prove a sufficient statistic, isolate the effect of the previous latent displacement, or establish sufficiency for physiological transitions or optimized behavioral decisions. Non-significant differences from observed trajectories are not equivalence evidence.

scope.time_horizon: Two observed weekly states at initialization, followed by propagated latent history

assertions.rationale: The individual's current and preceding encoded observations determine the initial displacement. That history then affects successive predictions through the propagated displacement and current latent state. This is explicit history conditioning, not evidence that the correct individual's history adds value beyond matched generic or swapped-history controls. The separate up-to-24-week coaching context must not be assigned to the SensorWM initialization.

No matched history-swap, individual-information withholding, population-prior, or analogous control tests whether the correct individual's physiological information adds predictive value without leakage. First-week versus trajectory comparisons vary information duration, not whether individual history is correct. Both coaching arms already receive participant-specific histories, and expert personalization ratings do not substitute for this predictive audit.

The rollout-location and displacement/path losses target trajectory prediction, and spectral normalization targets transition magnitude. The paper does not report an identity-specific memory, constraint, loss, or identity-preservation assessment. Per-participant initialization, linked trajectory plots and general prediction losses alone do not establish this feature. Physiological patient modeling does not make identity consistency inherently inapplicable.

assertions.value: Inspectable component-level contributions of named physiological and behavioral inputs to the explicit CHA readout
assertions.rationale: CHA exposes an explicit weighted log-hazard calculation with named input contributions, supporting inspection of the current-health readout. This assertion applies to the score component, not to SensorWM's latent coordinates. Interpretability does not establish causal explanations, calibrated individual risk, biological rejuvenation, or world-model membership for CHA.

value.mechanism: Explicit previous-state displacement retained alongside the current latent vector
value.equivalent_form: First-order Markov evolution in the augmented state
value.not_established: A long observation-history context or empirically demonstrated delayed-effect memory

assertions.rationale: Relative to the current latent observation representation z_t, the transition retains information about the preceding state through delta_z_t. This is a specified short history mechanism, even though the augmented state is Markov. The up-to-24-week history supplied to coaching and effort estimation is not evidence that SensorWM directly retains 24 weeks of observed state–action history.

value.conditioning_operation: The supplied action vector enters g(z_t,a_t), which produces the transition operator.

assertions.rationale: Actions are explicitly separated from physiological states, supplied to the transition during evaluated forecasts, and replaceable with prespecified alternatives. Forecast evaluation conditions on recorded future behavior; alternative inputs produce model-implied projections rather than identified causal intervention effects.

scope.time_horizon: Candidate behavioral sequences over the proposed 12-week plan

assertions.rationale: The operational vocabulary identifies volitional behavioral actions and distinguishes them from modeled physiological responses and score outcomes. The action–outcome firewall preserves those semantics during plan generation. Multiple unused therapeutic, acquisition, procedural or operational categories are not required for a single-role behavioral system. The physiology channel describes the model's intended response semantics, not proof of causal control; LLM text generation is not established as a communication action input to SensorWM.

scope.time_horizon: Weekly model inputs and proposed 12-week behavioral scenarios

assertions.rationale: The behavioral quantities, individual target, units and temporal context are sufficiently specified to interpret scenario queries. Sleep minutes in the model and hours in the coaching prompt are distinct representations, not interchangeable numerical inputs. This assessment does not establish complete candidate-grid reproducibility, safe execution, or causal dose–response validity.

scope.time_horizon: Time-indexed weekly behavioral sequences over the proposed 12-week scenario horizon

assertions.rationale: An action vector is supplied at each weekly transition, and prespecified alternative sequences can replace recorded future actions. This establishes a time-indexed query schedule rather than an untimed global condition. The LLM's three four-week coaching phases are a separate output structure; the source does not establish that every phased recommendation is re-simulated as its exact execution schedule.

scope.population: WEAR-ME profiles receiving hypothetical sleep, movement or combined pathways

assertions.rationale: The paper represents three behaviors jointly and describes combined pathways and sequence replacement. It does not sufficiently document which linked behavioral components must remain coherent, how omitted or unchanged fields are inherited, or how joint combinations preserve clinical or empirical dependencies. A multicomponent vector alone does not establish bundle semantics. No universal requirement that all three behaviors change together is inferred.

value.candidate_eligibility: Projected benefit greater than 0.1 CHA years

assertions.rationale: Explicit restrictions operate on candidate generation/selection, including a sleep-target cap and separation of volitional targets from physiological outcomes. The effort denominator floors and effort penalty are not themselves hard upper action bounds. Constraint existence does not establish comprehensive contraindication coverage, validated clinical thresholds, or successful safety enforcement.

Actions have explicit behavioral meanings—step targets, sleep duration and cardio-intensity minutes—and map to quantities communicated in coaching prescriptions rather than uninterpreted latent edits. This is semantic grounding for research queries and recommendations, not demonstrated participant execution, sustainable feasibility, or a validated causal response.

Historical per-action variability and peaks inform effort and feasibility, but no tested context-conditioned coverage, joint-regimen overlap, positivity diagnostic or mechanistic support criterion is reported for the queried alternatives. Individual historical ranges do not establish support for sustained combinations or for their predicted physiological consequences. This is insufficient reporting, not proof that every proposed regimen lacks support.

value.comparison_type: Same initial physiological history with alternative behavioral sequences
value.alternatives: Status quo and modified sleep, movement or combined pathways
value.reported_output: Projected trajectories and CHA endpoints used for ranking

assertions.rationale: The methods hold physiological initialization fixed while replacing actions, and reported examples compare optimized and maximum-reduction projections. This satisfies functional matched alternative-action comparison. Its physiological effect accuracy is not tested against observed outcomes under both alternatives; identified causal effects and individual counterfactual truth are not established.

scope.environment_kind: Offline recommendations concerning possible subsequent human behavior

assertions.rationale: Clinician reviews assess exercise intensity and plausibility, but no explicit assessment of reversibility, residual physiological harm, or recovery after adverse responses is reported. Offline generation does not make this question categorically inapplicable to advice intended to influence behavior, and stopping or revising a plan would not necessarily undo its physical consequences.

The augmented latent state carries current position and previous displacement; a transition updates it to subsequent physiological weeks and is evaluated through decoded forecasts. This is health-world temporal evolution, not optimization time or repeated calculation of CHA. Forecasting performance is mixed across features, and pooled results do not establish a tolerance-defined effective horizon.

assertions.value: Learned transition; mechanistic–learned hybrid status is assessed separately.
assertions.rationale: The predictor generating the state/action-dependent operator is trained jointly with the encoder using recursive latent rollout and displacement losses. Thus learning acts on the transition itself, not only on an encoder attached to fixed dynamics. Reported forecasting experiments establish execution, without independent code verification.

scope.time_horizon: Recursive weekly forecasts conditional on recorded future behavioral actions

assertions.rationale: The transition operator explicitly consumes settable behavioral vectors through adaptive layer normalization and a multiplicative action gate. Forecasting uses recorded future actions, and alternative-sequence queries are supported. These are conditional physiological forecasts, not forecasts of unknown future behavior or identified effects of prescribing actions.

scope.time_horizon: Specified recursive transition after latent-state initialization

assertions.rationale: The fully described recursive update computes F=g(z,a), the next displacement FΔz, and the next position z+FΔz without a sampled innovation or non-degenerate conditional transition distribution. Absence is scoped to this transition mechanism, not all randomness in training or LLM generation. Conditional-probability notation, encoder dropout, random SIGReg projections and the aggregate Gaussian representation target do not establish stochastic next-state dynamics.

value.structure: State/action-dependent linear transformation of the previous latent displacement, followed by discrete integration

assertions.rationale: Under this feature's combined mechanistic/structural definition, the imposed second-order displacement rule is an operational structural bias: successors are constrained through transformation of the previous displacement rather than independently generated. For example, the written equations retain zero displacement when the preceding displacement is exactly zero. This is not evidence of a physiological law, pharmacological sign constraint, conservation principle, or validated biological mechanism. CHA's epidemiological readout is not treated as a constraint on transition learning.

The inspected transition consists of a learned encoder/predictor with a generic displacement-integration structure and latent training losses; no separately specified physiological mechanistic component is coupled into that transition. Generic discrete integration does not make it a mechanistic–learned physiological hybrid. The downstream CHA formula combines epidemiological associations with predicted measurements but does not supply a mechanistic transition, so the broader composition does not establish this feature for SensorWM.

Trajectory Transformer and LeWorldModel-inspired formulations are compared during model selection, after which the latter is adopted. The paper does not report exchanging at least two backends under a documented common state/action/time/output contract or integration-testing such replacement with the same decoder and planner. Model-family comparisons and matched downstream classifiers do not establish pluggability.

scope.time_horizon: Single weekly transition grid in the specified SensorWM implementation

assertions.rationale: The complete specified transition advances one augmented latent physiological state on a common weekly grid. Minute-level and daily source measurements are aggregated before modeling rather than maintained as interacting dynamical levels with cross-scale mappings. Separate quarterly CHA analyses, multiple physiological domains, and the 12-week planning horizon do not constitute coupled multiscale dynamics. Absence is limited to this implemented transition configuration.

scope.time_horizon: 12-week training windows with two observed initialization states

criteria_met: Predicted latent states and displacements feed successive transitions after initialization.
The rollout loss compares recursively predicted latent locations with encoded observed targets across valid transitions.
The path loss compares predicted and observed latent displacements.
Encoder and transition predictor are jointly optimized under the combined rollout, path and SIGReg objective.
assertions.rationale: The reported training algorithm traverses multiple generated transitions rather than independent one-step targets. Future observed states supply loss targets, not teacher-forced transition inputs. Feature-specific effectiveness is not isolated by a reported loss ablation.

The documented SensorWM algorithm repeatedly applies one primitive weekly transition. Its augmented second-order state is memory, not a hierarchy of transition durations. Weekly aggregation, longer historical summaries, and the language-generated three-phase coaching schedule do not introduce coordinated higher/lower-level dynamics or variable-duration options. Absence is scoped to the described SensorWM transition configuration.

criteria_met: A post hoc linear mapping converts latent states into wearable physiological quantities.
The decoder is trained with masked observation-space mean-squared error while the encoder and transition predictor remain frozen.
Decoded future measurements are compared with observed measurements using feature-level forecasting metrics.
assertions.rationale: Latent-only world-model pretraining does not imply absence of a decoder in the evaluated system. This decoder is a separately trained diagnostic/readout component. Its training-data separation from final forecasting evaluation remains incompletely documented, and forecasting advantages are not uniform across features.

scope.time_horizon: Label/status classification from trajectories; no incident-disease prediction horizon established

criteria_met: Matched GRU sequence classifiers map observed or generated trajectories to named condition, laboratory, behavioral and medication labels.
Targets include diabetes, HOMA-IR-defined insulin resistance, hypertension and medication-use categories.
Participant-level test partitions and task-specific AUROC results are reported.

gate_assessments.rationale: Pretraining-statistic normalization, valid-day aggregation and participant-level downstream splits are documented. Decoder-training provenance, forecasting partition details, informative missingness, and full action/state timing semantics remain insufficiently specified.

Implemented learned state transitions and recursive future-prediction results are established. A separately identifiable one-step evaluation, its non-leaky decoder reference and a task-specific acceptance protocol are not sufficiently reported. Functional forecasting evidence is not denied by this unresolved stronger gate.

Recursive multistep use is explicit, but no quantitative error-versus-horizon curve, tolerance-defined effective horizon or horizon enforcement is established. Pooled feature metrics do not establish all 12 weeks as a validated horizon.

The scoped evaluated output is a point forecast without a claimed predictive-coverage guarantee or uncertainty-dependent decision rule. SIGReg, metric standard errors and multiple alternative action plans are not predictive uncertainty. This does not waive uncertainty requirements for a future clinical decision-support release.

Settable actions, parameterization and matched origins are demonstrated. The full candidate grid, joint feasibility/support, daily/weekly unit conventions and regimen-update details are not complete enough for an assurance pass.

Authors explicitly decline identified causal-effect interpretation. An identified-effect gate is inapplicable to that narrowly labeled research claim. User-facing benefit/payoff language is separately flagged and must not inherit this exemption.

scope.interpretation: User-facing numerical benefits or therapeutic-effect assurance

gate_assessments.rationale: The communication prompt asks for exact projected payoffs while suppressing model/simulation terminology. No identification strategy, causal assumptions, interventional reference or confounding sensitivity establishes those numbers as effects of following a plan.

Model-coupled candidate optimization and decision-output evaluation are present. No independent model-mismatch/reward-exploitation test or action-space coverage study is established. Observed redundant steps and optimistic projections motivate, but do not substitute for, that test.

Some filters and prompt guardrails exist, but validated contraindication coverage, abstention/fallback, escalation and appropriate uncertainty disclosure are not established. Expert safe-intensity endorsement is neither zero failures nor demonstrated operational safety.

Separate-cohort and age/BMI/sex subgroup analyses are reported, with task-specific degradations. Decoder adaptation, overlap controls, independent composition transfer and subgroup acceptance criteria are insufficient for a complete pass.

scope.gate_purpose: Establish that a defined actual-human expert review of generated plans was performed
scope.population: 49 retrospective profiles; five coaches and five clinicians

gate_assessments.rationale: Actual human expert participation (5 certified lifestyle coaches and 5 board-certified clinicians evaluating 49 paired plans) is documented and supports R4. Broader G10 assurance remains unresolved (downgraded from pass) because outcomes are mixed: substantial rater heterogeneity (Coach 2 adherence win rate 44.9%), nonzero unfavorable clinician safety (2/245) and 12-week biological plausibility (34/245) ratings, non-independent repeated rating-level tests across 49 profiles, and absence of prospective user delivery or realized adherence.

The reported experiment explicitly does not deliver the system prospectively to users and does not claim measured realized adherence or patient benefit. Prospective utility is future work. The gate would be unresolved for any future claim of live utility.

No operational product/version release for clinical use is documented. A code-release promise is not operational deployment. Governance and monitoring would require new evidence before such a release.

limitations: Automated API model review, including a skeptical second-pass synthesis of supplied automated page reviews; no independent human review, replication, code execution or clinical verification.

All 97 supplied text pages were reviewed. Visual observations derive from supplied automated page-image notes; this call had no directly inspectable page images. Direct visual reinspection remains necessary for image-dependent conflicts and scientific interpretation.
The supplied PDF hash and local availability are provenance claims from the source record, not newly computed or filesystem-verified facts.
Feature assertions are intentionally empty at the user's request. This is not a completed 128-feature annotation and must not be admitted as feature-complete without the separate feature pass.
No JSON Schema validator, semantic validation engine, repository access, graph assembly or filesystem write was executed in this call.
SensorWM is an implemented learned healthcare transition method as reported in executed experiments, not a static health-age regressor. Its causal and clinical validity remain separate questions.
Forecast evaluation supplies recorded future actions. Baselines' access to equivalent future-action information is not established, limiting interpretation of comparative forecasting gains.

Decoder-training provenance, its observation-level 15% validation split and separation from the forecasting test set are insufficiently detailed, despite explicit participant-level downstream classifier splits.

The headline average R² does not define feature weighting, exact sample denominator, forecast-step aggregation or uncertainty. Supplementary per-feature results include failures to outperform simple baselines.

Reported 12-week windows, two-state initialization, available 24-week histories and 12-week future coaching plans are different temporal quantities. The exact maximum unobserved forecast span is not fully resolved.
No tolerance-defined effective horizon, quantitative error-versus-horizon validation or clinical horizon enforcement is established.

SIGReg's Gaussian aggregate target, training dropout, repeated evaluation runs and alternative plans do not establish predictive uncertainty, epistemic/aleatoric decomposition or trajectory calibration.
The displacement transition has an absorbing zero-displacement case under the written equations. Its empirical frequency and effects are not tested in the supplied results.

No held-out experimental behavioral intervention or identified individual counterfactual reference validates the alternative-action projections. Authors explicitly acknowledge time-varying confounding.

Historical variability and peaks are proxies for effort and feasibility, not validated current safety, sustainable adherence or joint-action support. The complete candidate grid and all bounds are not supplied.
The 0.1-year minimum projected benefit and behavioral-variability floors are author-selected optimization policies, not independently established clinically meaningful or universally safe thresholds.

CHA combines associations for different endpoints and populations with a mortality-derived age-rate constant. Correlation discounting does not establish an outcome-calibrated joint risk model or causal adjustment.

CHA and mod-LE8 share wearable components. Construct alignment is not wholly independent validation. Optional domains and unadjusted versus collinearity-adjusted CHA require configuration-specific interpretation.
All of Us disease association is a prognostic analysis of existing records; it is not prospective deployment of SensorWM or the coaching system.

All of Us eligibility, informative wear/censoring, recorded-diagnosis timing, daily-minimum-heart-rate proxy and complete-case selection may affect estimates. Causal effects are not established by temporal lag or adjustment for age, sex and BMI.
The complete coaching comparator adds CHA, status-quo projections, ranked options and differing content instructions together. It does not isolate the causal contribution of learned dynamics.

Human ratings reuse 49 profiles and five raters per track. Stated rating-level exact tests and Wilson intervals do not establish independence across cases and raters; human rubric multiplicity handling is incomplete.
The five personas cover 1,079 of 2,780 profiles, not the entire cohort. Recent evaluated snapshots and habitual persona-selection summaries differ, and some eligibility labels require clarification.
Expert-rated anticipated adherence is not actual adherence. Safe-intensity endorsement and plausibility ratings are not adverse-event evidence, noninferiority, effectiveness or authorization.
Rater heterogeneity is substantial. A claim of uniform adherence-preference direction conflicts with one coach's reported 44.9% Counterfactual win rate.
Reported failures include redundant steps for already active users, ambiguous incremental-step wording, overly optimistic adaptation timescales and nonzero unfavorable safety/plausibility ratings.

Several downstream tasks and subgroups lose discrimination. Small positive counts, broad confidence intervals and absent multiplicity/equivalence protocols preclude broad preservation or fairness guarantees.
Supplied visual notes report larger correlation discrepancies than the manuscript's qualitative narrative suggests. Direct image confirmation is required before a definitive image-based conclusion.
The thyroid-medication subgroup P-value differs between supplied text and the supplied visual-review note. Both values are retained pending direct-source verification.

Automated plan evaluation uses the same named primary model family as generation, supplies model projections as legitimate judging context, and exhibits ceiling effects. It is not independent human or clinical corroboration.
The prompts suppress model/simulation terminology while requesting exact payoffs. Appropriate uncertainty communication and reliance calibration are not established.
No prospective silent use, intervention trial, realized patient benefit, actual-care safety evaluation or regulated deployment is established for the reported coaching system.

Code is promised upon publication, not verified released. Model weights, asset licenses, executable configurations, training compute and latency are not reported sufficiently. Private Fitbit data limit reproducibility.
